title: Run the Privacy Filter model in the commit gate, configurable per machine and repo
description:
Run the Privacy Filter model inside the commit gate, so a secret the pattern rules miss is blocked before the commit exists. Configurable per machine and per repository. Off unless a person turns it on.

## Measured basis (Mac, 10 cores, 34 GB, leftblock 0.9.0 deep.py)
Weights 2.6 GB. Resident memory after scanning 3.3 GB. Importing torch and transformers 3.4 s (15.3 s first run). Loading weights 1.4-1.9 s. A 2,000-character chunk takes about 2.3 s on CPU; the Mac GPU was slower (3.2 s), so stay on CPU. Added text per commit over 702 real commits: median 1,250 characters, p90 34,000, max 500,000. So a resident server removes about 5 s of startup from every commit; scan time still scales with added text.

## Configuration: Git config, nothing new on disk
Read with `git config --get` from the repository being committed, so `--global` sets a machine default, a plain `git config` sets one repository, and `git -c leftblock.deep.mode=off commit` covers one commit. Nothing is committed to the repository.

- `leftblock.deep.mode`: `off` (default) | `resident` | `per-commit`. `resident` uses the server below. `per-commit` loads the model in the hook process each time, with no server, for machines that cannot spare the memory between commits.
- `leftblock.deep.onUnavailable`: `block` (default) | `warn`. What happens when the mode is on but the extra or model is missing, or the server cannot start. `warn` prints a warning and lets the commit continue; `block` is the same failure path as chapter 11 failing closed, with no override offered.
- `leftblock.deep.idleMinutes`: default 60; 0 means never exit. Only applies to `resident`.
- `leftblock.deep.labels`, `leftblock.deep.threshold`: same meaning and validation as the existing deep-scan options.
- An invalid value blocks with a message naming the key. It never silently falls back.

## Commit gate
Add the model as one more result inside `_run_configured_checks`, so `check` (local pre-commit hook) and `hook` (receipt mode) both get it through `run_checks`. Result name `privacy-filter`, findings use the existing deep finding shape, added before overrides are applied so `.leftblock-allow.yml` entries work. Always run it even if gitleaks found something, so one attempt reports everything. Honour the merge-scoped index: during a merge read additions with the same env the checkers get (`staged_additions` needs an env argument). A finding blocks exactly like a gitleaks finding, never prints the value, and the printed override command must work for deep findings and for a mix of both kinds (`leftblock allow --deep` handles deep ids today). `allow --deep` and `deep-scan` use the configured labels, threshold and, in resident mode, the server, so recording an override does not load a second model. The hook process must not import torch or transformers in resident mode, and in mode `off` must do no deep work at all (no new imports, no extra git processes beyond reading the mode).

## Resident server
New module `leftblock/server.py`, modelled on Virtuus's `python/src/virtuus/service.py`: JSON lines over a Unix domain socket, one request per connection.
- Protocol: `ping` returns protocol version, leftblock version, model and revision. `detect` takes `{"text": ...}` and returns `[[start, end, label, score], ...]`. `stop` exits. A `ServerDetector` callable returns the same `detect(text) -> spans` shape, so `deep.scan` and `deep.scan_text` do not change.
- Location: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/leftblock/` if set, else `~/.cache/leftblock/run/`. Directory mode 0700, socket 0600. Refuse to use the directory if another user owns it or it is group or world accessible. Staged text travels over this socket, so this is a privacy requirement. Socket name includes the leftblock version, so an upgrade starts a new server and the old one idles out. Keep the path short enough for the platform's socket path limit.
- Just-in-time start: connect; on failure take an flock on a lock file beside the socket, re-check, then spawn `sys.executable -I -B -m leftblock.cli deep-server serve` detached (`start_new_session=True`, stdio to a log file holding lifecycle events only). Concurrent commits must start exactly one server. Remove a stale socket only while holding the lock.
- Waiting: no fixed timeout. The client waits for as long as the server process is alive and fails as unavailable if it exits, printing one notice that the model is loading. A request in progress waits the same way.
- One lock around the pipeline, so concurrent commits queue rather than compete. The server's accept loop stays threaded so `ping` and `stop` answer during a scan.
- The server must never log, store or echo request text or spans. Log only start, ready, idle exit and error type names.
- Idle exit after `idleMinutes` with no `detect`, then remove the socket.
- Never download in a hook: load with `local_files_only=True`. Model absent means unavailable, and the message says to run `leftblock deep-server download`, which fetches it and says how large it is.
- Pin the weights: add `deep.MODEL_REVISION = "7ffa9a043d54d1be65afb281eddf0ffbe629385b"` for the server, per-commit mode and download. Leave the eval harness as it is. Stay on CPU.
- `LEFTBLOCK_DEEP_DETECTOR` must keep working through the server process (it inherits the environment), so specs exercise the real socket with the stub detector.
- Where `AF_UNIX` is unavailable (Windows), `resident` is treated as unavailable with a message saying to use `per-commit`.
- CLI: `leftblock deep-server serve|status|stop|download`.

## Docs and specs
- New `features/21_model_scan_in_the_commit_gate.feature`, narrative like the other chapters. Cover: off by default and no deep work; each mode blocks a flagged commit and passes a clean one, in `check` and in receipt `hook`; recorded override passes; value never printed; onUnavailable block and warn; invalid config blocks; per-repo config beats global; `git -c` for one commit; second commit reuses the running server (same pid); concurrent first commits start one server; idle exit; socket and directory permissions; unsafe directory refused; server not logging text; merge scope.
- Rewrite the chapter 17 intro and the README passages saying the hook never runs the model (lines near 7, 22, 32, 367 onward, and the mermaid diagram) and document the settings table, memory and disk costs, and the measured timings above with their caveat. Keep the `leftblock[deep]` line in pyproject accurate.
- CI fails on skipped scenarios; run `python -m unittest discover tests` and `behave`.
